title: New heavens and a new earth
author: Isaiah
lines: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth;
and the former things will not be remembered,
why: The Bible's first promise of a new creation, spoken to people living among the ruins of Jerusalem after the exile. It does not promise escape from the world but a world remade, and the Bible's last chapters take up its words. Say it when the news is bad, or when your own past weighs on you: the former things will not be remembered.

title: The Alpha and the Omega
author: Revelation
lines: “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God,
“who is and who was and who is to come,
why: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet. Written by a prisoner on Patmos to churches under pressure, this verse says that the God who began the story will end it, and is with us in the middle: who is, who was, and who is to come. Say it when history, or your own life, seems out of anyone's control.

title: Watch, keep alert, and pray
author: Mark
lines: for you don’t know when the time is.
why: Jesus's disciples asked when the end would come. This was his answer: not a date, but a way of living. Watching is not staring at the sky; it is being found faithful in the work you have been given. Say it at the start of a day, or before a task you would rather avoid.
